text:
Priya: heads-up — I need to drop at 23:00 PT, can someone flip primary for the overnight window (23:00–07:00)? There's a lingering Sev2 on embeds with increased tail p95 and a small page queue. I've left notes in the runbook but want to handoff context here.

Liam: I can take primary for that window. quick question — is the page noise stable or still spiking?

Meera: pinging incident-bot for the latest page history and any open alerts — we should confirm if it needs escalation.

incident-bot: Pager event: sev2 "embeds-high-p95" active, 4 pages in last 15m, last ack: none. Current alerting policy: tiered -> primary then secondary -> paging-radar. Docs: https://redwood.example/runbooks/embeds

Priya: thanks. Noise has come down a bit after a cache tweak but tails still creep at high token counts for some requests. I left a quick checklist in runbook under "overnight-handback":

```
- Check embeddings-kv cache hitrate: dashboard -> infra/embeds/cache
- If p95 > 800ms: disable large-batch-reads experiment (flag: embeddings.large_batch_reads=false)
- Restart replica set if ASG memory > 85% for 10m: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/embeds-svc -n inference`
- If 5+ pages within 30m escalate to secondary and start s3-scoop.
```

Priya: added a quick log snippet where we saw the spike:

```
2025-08-12T22:41:03Z embeds-7f8b9c: WARN tail-latency token_count=4096 p95=1234ms backend=kv-store-2
2025-08-12T22:41:04Z embeds-7f8b9c: ERROR read-timeout backend=kv-store-2 retry=1
```

Jamal: tagging in — if you take primary Liam, make sure the rate-limit overrides are set for the PLG paths (/embed/batch). Otherwise customer-facing latency goes through the roof.

Liam: got it. I'll:
- ack pager in PD
- set rate-limit override to 120 rps for /embed/batch
- monitor cache hitrate and p95 dash for 30m
- post updates in this thread every 15m or on change

Meera: can you also confirm who is secondary for the night? I can be secondary after 01:00 if needed but I have a deploy scheduled at 00:30 — prefer not to be secondary during that window.

Liam: secondary = Jamal for the 23:00–07:00 window? Jamal, ok for you to be secondary + shadow?

Jamal: I can be secondary until 03:00, then switch to Meera at 03:00 if needed. So plan: Liam primary 23:00–07:00, Jamal secondary 23:00–03:00, Meera backup 03:00–07:00.

Priya: perfect — can you all confirm handoff steps so on-call logs are consistent? I put a short template in the runbook under "handoff-note". Copying it here:

```
Handoff note template:
- Primary: <name> (start/end)
- Secondary: <name> (start/end)
- Active incidents: list (link to PD)
- Quick state: cache/hitrate/queue_depth/p95
- Actions taken: list commands + results
- Next check-in: timestamp
```

Liam: confirmed. I'll paste the first handoff note when I take primary. Also I'll run a sanity command right now: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=embeds -o wide` and check logs with `stern embeds -n inference --since 10m`.

incident-bot: Reminder: If paging rate > 5 in 30m automatically escalate to secondary. Current count: 4 in 15m.

Meera: FYI for whoever is primary — if you escalate to secondary and still see high p95 after the large-batch toggle, there is a mitigation to shadow route 10% of heavy requests to a smaller model to buy time (details in runbook).

Liam: noted. I'll also open a lightweight incident postmortem stub in our incidents tracker so we can fill after the window.

Priya: thanks everyone. Liam — if you run into anything that looks like data loss or new error classes, escalate immediately. Otherwise a simple handoff post when you take over is fine. See you all tomorrow AM. :wave:

Liam: taking primary now — handoff note posted (link: https://redwood.example/handoffs/1749876543). I'll update every 15m or on change. :thumbsup:

Jamal: shadowing confirmed. I'll watch the PD queue and be ready to ramp to 100% if needed.

Meera: on-call coverage acknowledged. Good luck and ping if you need extra eyes.

incident-bot: Pager acknowledged by Liam. Escalation window active.

Liam: quick status (T+10m): cache hitrate 78%, p95 720ms, 0 new pages in last 10m. continuing watch.
